audit_findings.title: Forecast capital intensity may be materially above the owner-earnings baseline
audit_findings.magnitude: 2026 forecast capex $190.0 million, $89.3 million above 2025 capex of $100.7 million and equal to 85.5% of the $104.5 million anchor OE; first-half 2026 capex was $90.0 million versus $52.0 million in first-half 2025
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring maintenance capital expenditure reduces forecast owner earnings and therefore both the explicit-period cash flows and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect our capital expenditures to remain at, or slightly above, 9% of revenu e for 2026 , as we plan to continue to build, reshape and maintain additional data center equipment capacity in all regions and we keep investing in our Commerce Intelligence Platform.
audit_findings.explanation: The spending increase is filed and already occurring, although the record does not separate maintenance from growth capex. If a substantial part of the $89.3 million increase is recurring maintenance, it is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion because it is nearly as large as the entire OE anchor.
audit_findings.action: Obtain management or asset-level evidence separating 2026 maintenance, replacement, committed capacity, and discretionary growth capex; rerun OE and all scenarios using the recurring maintenance portion.

audit_findings.title: The bridge appears to treat all cash as excess despite operating-liquidity needs
audit_findings.magnitude: $280.288 million bridge exposure, equal to $5.03 per diluted share and 16.0% of base equity value; the required operating-cash deduction is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for working capital, restricted balances, seasonal funding, commitments, or continued operations must be excluded from the excess-cash equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash at December 31, 2025 were held for working capital and general corporate purposes, which could include acquisitions, and amounted to $342.4 million as of December 31, 2025 .
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation demonstrably adds the full $280.288 million balance, while the filing states cash is held for working capital and general corporate purposes. The distributable portion is unresolved, but the gross exposure exceeds the $4.33 per-share gap between the $21.95 buy-below threshold and the $17.62 market price, so it can change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Establish minimum operating cash from monthly liquidity troughs, working-capital seasonality, restricted or trapped balances, contractual commitments, and management treasury policy; rerun the bridge with only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated cash-flow components may not match the parent-common share denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: June 2026 NCI carrying value $36.616 million; 2025 net income attributable to NCI $4.777 million; first-half 2026 NCI income $1.324 million; full valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated D&A, capex, working-capital flows, and cash may include amounts attributable to the 34% noncontrolling ownership of Criteo KK, while per-share value belongs only to parent shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Criteo S.A. and its subsidiaries where we have controlling financial interests.
audit_findings.explanation: The ownership mismatch is a valid unresolved possibility, but the supplied record does not show which OE components were consolidated versus parent-attributable or the fair value of the NCI claim. The reported NCI carrying value is only 2.1% of base equity value, but carrying value is not sufficient to establish the economic adjustment, so materiality cannot be resolved.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every OE component and bridge item on a parent-attributable basis; alternatively value consolidated operations consistently and deduct a supported fair value for the noncontrolling claim.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may not reflect the known customer curtailment run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 customer revenue approximately $97.245 million, computed as 5% of $1,944.901 million; first-half 2026 Retail Media contribution ex-TAC fell $31.042 million or 26%, while total adjusted EBITDA fell $43.330 million or 24%; customer-specific OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A post-curtailment perimeter or run-rate adjustment would reduce anchor OE and possibly the assumed growth path before discounting.
audit_findings.evidence: As previously disclosed, our largest customer notified us that they will curtail the scope of future services commencing November 1, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: Only two months of the disclosed curtailment could affect 2025, yet the valuation uses a 2025-based historical anchor with no perimeter adjustment. The subsequent filing confirms significant 2026 deterioration and attributes Retail Media weakness to scope changes with two clients. Although the largest customer's precise margin contribution is unavailable, the filed scale and current-period decline make the issue reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the customer's 2025 revenue, contribution margin, associated operating costs, 2026 retained scope, and replacement wins; calculate the annualized parent-attributable OE loss and rerun the anchor with an explicit perimeter adjustment.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized SBC may bypass the stated no-add-back rail
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.8 million for 2025, equal to 5.6% of anchor OE; if treated conservatively as a recurring full reduction to the anchor, computed base operating value impact is approximately $81.5 million or $1.46 per share, and the 30% MOS threshold impact is approximately $1.02 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized SBC can escape current compensation expense and then be neutralized if related software amortization is added back, overstating OE despite use of a diluted share denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: (1) The periods ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 , are presented net of $ 5.8 million and $ 4.0 million , respectively, capitalized stock-based compensation relating to internally developed software.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the $5.8 million was separately deducted is unresolved, but even the conservative computed case that reduces the full anchor by that amount would lower the $21.95 buy-below threshold to approximately $20.93, still above the $17.62 market price. On the supplied numbers, this finding alone does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace capitalized SBC through each historical OE reconciliation, confirm a separate deduction of total SBC, and rerun if the $5.8 million was omitted or associated amortization was added back.

audit_findings.title: A noncash tax-allowance release may remain in FY2025 owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.7 million, equal to 9.3% of anchor OE; conservatively treating the full amount as an anchor reduction gives a computed base operating value impact of approximately $136.2 million or $2.44 per share, and a 30% MOS threshold impact of approximately $1.71 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: An unreversed noncash tax benefit would inflate FY2025 OE and could raise the log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2025 , the Company released a valuation allowance of approximately $ 9.7 million related to deferred tax assets in the United Kingdom, primarily as a result of sustained profitability.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not establish that the release survived the OE reconciliation, and a cash-flow-based build may already reverse it. Even assuming the entire $9.7 million reduces the anchor—not merely the latest observation—the buy-below threshold would be approximately $20.24, still above the $17.62 market price. This supplies a concrete upper-bound comparison showing that the item alone is not material to the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $9.7 million valuation-allowance release through net income, deferred-tax adjustments, and the FY2025 OE reconciliation; correct the series and recompute the log trend if it was retained.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2022 residual D&A $61.2 million, equal to 40.8% of filed FY2022 D&A; eligible portion and anchor effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A demonstrated to be non-economic and eligible would be added back to historical OE, potentially increasing the log-trend anchor and scenario values.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2022 $61.2m (40.8% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The current treatment is conservative and cannot overstate value. The $61.2 million residual is large relative to FY2022 OE of $55.4 million, but the record does not establish that any portion is eligible or how reclassification of one historical year would change the log-trend anchor. Materiality therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the filed D&A composition by asset class and reconcile it to maintenance capex and OE policy; rerun the historical series and trend only for components supported as eligible non-economic add-backs.
